title: Boss: audit the pipeline
summary: Scan a repository and its workflows the way a security reviewer would.

steps.title: The audit
steps.body: Security asked for an automated review of every repository: committed secrets, over-powered tokens, unpinned actions and a severity gate for dependencies. Build each check.

steps.title: Committed secrets
prompt: Write `List<int> FindSecretLines(string[] lines)` returning the **1-based** numbers of lines that look like secrets. A line matches when it contains:
- an AWS access key id: `AKIA` followed by 16 uppercase letters or digits
- a GitHub token: `ghp_` followed by 36 letters or digits
- `password`, `secret` or `api_key`/`apikey` (any case), then optional spaces, `:` or `=`, optional spaces, then a **quoted** value
A reference such as `password: ${{ secrets.DB }}` is not quoted, so it is fine. `System.Text.RegularExpressions` is imported.
hints: Keep the three regexes in an array and test each line against `Any` of them.
In a verbatim string, a double quote is written `""`. The third pattern: `(?i)(password|secret|api_?key)\s*[:=]\s*[""'][^""']+[""']`.
template: Dojo.Eq("finds the four real secrets", new List<int> { 1, 3, 4, 6 }, FindSecretLines(dojoLines));
Dojo.Eq("short ghp_ strings are not tokens", new List<int>(), FindSecretLines(new[] { "ghp_short" }));
steps.explain: Real scanners (GitHub secret scanning, gitleaks) use hundreds of such patterns plus entropy checks, and can block the push itself.

steps.title: Over-powered tokens
prompt: Write `List<string> ExcessPermissions(Dictionary<string, string> granted, Dictionary<string, string> needed)`. Levels are `none` < `read` < `write`;
a scope missing from `needed` needs `none`. For every granted scope above what is needed, return `"scope: granted (needs level)"`,
granted `{contents: write, packages: write}`, needed `{contents: read}` → `"contents: write (needs read)"`, `"packages: write (needs none)"`.
starter: List<string> ExcessPermissions(Dictionary<string, string> granted, Dictionary<string, string> needed)
solution: List<string> ExcessPermissions(Dictionary<string, string> granted, Dictionary<string, string> needed)
hints: Turn levels into numbers: none 0, read 1, write 2.
template: Dojo.Eq("the example", new List<string> { "contents: write (needs read)", "packages: write (needs none)" },
Dojo.Eq("exactly right", new List<string>(), ExcessPermissions(new() { ["contents"] = "read", ["id-token"] = "write" }, new() { ["contents"] = "read", ["id-token"] = "write" }));
Dojo.Eq("less than needed is not excess", new List<string>(), ExcessPermissions(new() { ["contents"] = "read" }, new() { ["contents"] = "write" }));
Dojo.Eq("read nobody needs", new List<string> { "issues: read (needs none)" }, ExcessPermissions(new() { ["issues"] = "read" }, new()));

steps.title: Unpinned actions
prompt: Write `List<string> Unpinned(string[] workflowLines)`. For each line containing `uses:`, take the value after it (trimmed, and without any
trailing `# comment`). Ignore local actions starting with `./` and `docker://` references. Report every remaining `owner/repo@ref`
whose `ref` is not exactly **40 lowercase hex characters**, in file order. `System.Text.RegularExpressions` is imported.

This is a deliberately simple text scan: treat **every** line that contains `uses:` this way, even a `run:` line that only mentions the word, and report a value with no `@` too (its ref is empty, so it is not pinned).
hints: `line[(at + 5)..]` is everything after `uses:`; split off the comment at `#` and trim.
The ref is after the last `@`; check it with `^[0-9a-f]{40}$`.
template: "      - run: echo uses: is just text here",
Dojo.Eq("finds unpinned references", new List<string> { "actions/setup-dotnet@v6", "some-org/deploy@main", "is just text here", "actions/cache@11bd719" }, Unpinned(dojoWf));
steps.explain: Notice the `run:` line: a text-based check flags it too. Real linters (zizmor, actionlint) parse the YAML instead of searching lines.

steps.title: Severity gate
prompt: Write `string SeverityGate(List<(string Package, string Severity)> findings, string failAt)`. Severities rank `low` < `moderate` < `high` < `critical`.
Findings at or above `failAt` block the build:
- otherwise → `"fail: "` followed by the blocking packages, sorted ordinally and de-duplicated, joined with `", "`
starter: string SeverityGate(List<(string Package, string Severity)> findings, string failAt)
solution: string SeverityGate(List<(string Package, string Severity)> findings, string failAt)
hints: The index in `[low, moderate, high, critical]` is the rank.
Filter, project to the package name, `Distinct`, sort, join.
template: var dojoF = new List<(string Package, string Severity)> { ("Serilog", "low"), ("System.Text.Json", "high"), ("Foo", "critical"), ("System.Text.Json", "moderate") };
Dojo.Eq("high and above", "fail: Foo, System.Text.Json", SeverityGate(dojoF, "high"));
Dojo.Eq("everything at low", "fail: Foo, Serilog, System.Text.Json", SeverityGate(dojoF, "low"));
